newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Guatemala peace process crisis deepens.
newsitem.headline: Guatemala peace process crisis deepens.

text.p: Guatemala's president on Thursday suspended a programme to disband paramilitary patrols during a crisis that has halted peace talks between the government and leftist rebels, an army official said.

"The commander-in-chief of the army has temporarily suspended the process of demobilizing and disarming the Civil Self-defence Patrols until the peace negotiations return to normal," army spokesman Colonel Otto Noack told Reuters.

The disbandment of the violent civil patrols was an important part of the delicate peace process, which stumbled badly on Monday when the government suspended peace talks after accusing guerrillas of kidnapping an elderly woman.

On Wednesday the Guatemalan National Revolutionary Unit (URNG) high command, in exile in Mexico City, released a statement recognising that a guerrilla commander had participated in a kidnapping, but denying the high command knew about the crime until the arrest.

United Nations moderator Jean Arnault, the go-between in the peace talks, said the talks were only postponed until Saturday. But the delay has put pressure on the tight schedule of the talks and has shaken confidence in the peace process.
The suspension of the civil patrol demobilization programme is a measure of the seriousness of the crisis.

The patrols, formed in the early 1980s during the height of Guatemala's brutal, 36-year civil war, were the eyes and ears of the army in many Indian villages. At their height, the patrols numbered 900,000 members.
The United Nations mission in Guatemala called the patrols one of the greatest perpetrators of human rights violations in the civil war.
